'''John Ewart McGrady''' (born 30 April 1968) is an English chemist and academic who previously played first-class [[cricket]] while a student at the [[University of Oxford]].

The son of the cricket administrator and [[Minor Counties of English and Welsh cricket|minor counties]] cricketer Albert McGrady, he was born in April 1968 at [[Ryton, Tyne and Wear|Ryton, County Durham]]. He later read chemistry at [[St Catherine's College, Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/31/31369/31369.html |title=Player profile: John McGrady |publisher=CricketArchive |accessdate=2020-06-11 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> While studying at Oxford, McGrady played [[first-class cricket]] for [[Oxford University Cricket Club|Oxford University]] in 1990, making six appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/31/31369/First-Class_Matches.html |title=First-Class Matches played by John McGrady |publisher=CricketArchive |accessdate=2020-06-11 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Playing as a [[wicket-keeper]], he scored 15 runs in these matches and made two [[stumpings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/31/31369/f_Batting_by_Team.html |title=First-Class Batting and Fielding For Each Team by John McGrady |publisher=CricketArchive |accessdate=2020-06-11 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

From Oxford, he studied for his [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate]] in Australia at the [[Australian National University]].<ref name="PRO">{{cite web|url=https://www.new.ox.ac.uk/node/1002 |title=John McGrady |publisher=www.new.ox.ac.uk |accessdate=2020-06-11}}</ref> He became a chemistry lecturer at the [[University of York]] in 1997, before lecturing at the [[University of Glasgow]] in 2006. In 2009 he returned to the University of Oxford, becoming a [[fellow]] at [[New College, Oxford|New College]].<ref name="PRO"/>
